This error indicates that one or more of your GPUs may have fallen off the bus or is not communicating properly. First, use nvidia-smi to verify all GPUs are being detected properly by the system. If a GPU is not listed, this is often a power supply issue such as a molten cable or faulty PSU. As a temporary fix, you can relist the machine, but this requires manual intervention and is not a permanent solution. On fresh installations, the error may sometimes resolve itself after waiting a few hours.

This error indicates a GPU bandwidth test failure where the GPU is not properly communicating with the system. The error occurs when one or more bandwidth tests (Host-to-Device, Device-to-Host, or Device-to-Device) fail. There are several potential causes and solutions:
Hardware Issues (most serious): GPU falling off the bus, power supply issues (unplugged or loose 12-pin power connector), or riser problems. Check dmesg -t output and verify nvidia-smi is working properly to diagnose.
Platform Issue: This may be a Vast.ai platform issue affecting multiple machines. Try restarting the Vast.ai daemon: sudo systemctl restart vastai
nvidia-container-toolkit Version Issue: The problem may be caused by nvidia-container-toolkit version causing GPU UUID problems. Downgrade nvidia-container-toolkit-base and nvidia-container-toolkit to version 1.15.0-1, then place a hold on these packages using apt to prevent automatic updates. Check vast kaalia logs at /var/lib/vastai_kaalia/kaalia.logX for errors around docker run commands.
when the GPU driver attempts to access the GPU over its PCI Express connection and finds that the GPU is not accessible.
